gaps: P0: none (the 1497 Nuremberg Chronicle woodcut #1 is an imaginary city with a dome and a statue column, not a true view of Trier)
notes: P1 alternative: #7, Merian’s view from Topographia Archiepiscopatuum Moguntinensis, Trevirensis et Coloniensis (1646; the file says 1648), a sharp black-and-white view; the colored Braun and Hogenberg was preferred and both fall in P1. #10 is catalogued as a copy (Hollstein Dutch 33-copy), apparently after Merian’s view; the city is a thin band, so it is on the weak side. P4 alternative: #18, Bain News Service photo from the Petrisberg about 1910 (very high resolution, cathedral prominent), but its date carries a doubt in the record. #15 is an Adolphe Braun stereo card, not Braun and Hogenberg; #19 is the blank back of a card; #20 is a painting of the cathedral and Church of Our Lady (Metz museum), not a general view.
